Karen (sales): Quick heads-up — ClearPathHealth POC hit a throughput ceiling this morning. They're seeing request queuing at peak and said burst credits are exhausted. Can we temporarily adjust their Dedicated pool for the POC window?

Ajay (eng-runtime): What are their current pool settings and target qps / seq lengths?

Karen (sales): Current: clearpath-poc-pool (dedicated) = reserved 4 nodes, autoscale max 6, burst enabled but credits at 0. Typical seq len ~ 512 tokens, bursty traffic hitting ~85 reqs/s, wanting <150ms p95. Need runway for demo tomorrow and heavy test day after — asking for reserved bump to 6 and +2 burst nodes for 48 hours.

Lucy (eng-platform): Ok — we can do a temporary reservation increase + extra burst capacity. We try to avoid long-lived manual bumps; suggest scheduled override for 48h then auto-revert. Example patch:```json
{
  "pool": "clearpath-poc-pool",
  "reserved_nodes": 6,
  "autoscale": { "min": 4, "max": 8 },
  "burst": { "enabled": true, "burst_nodes": 2, "credits_alloc": "manual" },
  "override_ttl": "48h"
}
```

Karen (sales): Can you estimate cost delta for that window? Need sign-off from finance. Also customer asked about scoped API keys for the POC to prevent cross-tenant risks.

Finance Bot: Rough calc: +2 reserved nodes for 48h on our current pricing ~ $2,400, plus burst usage variable — cap estimate with burst fully used ~ $3,800 for 48h. Approve up to $4k for one-off POC adjustments; anything above needs manager approval.

Taylor (customer-success): Recommend creating a scoped API key limited to clearpath-poc (models: small-gpt, permissions: generate, embeddings) and per-key rate limit 200r/s. That'll reduce blast risk and make cost easier to attribute.

Security Ops: Reminder: for Dedicated POCs we require IP allowlist + VPC peering checklist completed and KMS key for logs if customer asks. ClearPath signed the questionnaire but left blank the peering CID ranges — need that before we open extra capacity to them. @Karen (sales) can you follow up?

Karen (sales): I'll ping them now. For the immediate demo they said peering will be ready by EOD but will share CID ranges later today. Is it safe to schedule now with a conditional hold?

Ajay (eng-runtime): From runtime side it's low risk. We can stage the change as a scheduled job but gate activation on Security Ops flag (peeringOk=true). CLI for quick change:```
redwoodctl pools update --name clearpath-poc-pool --reserved 6 --autoscale-max 8 --burst 2 --override-ttl 48h
```Rollback:```
redwoodctl pools update --name clearpath-poc-pool --reserved 4 --autoscale-max 6 --burst 0
```

Provision Bot: Scheduled patch job created (job id: pj-20260308-001). Waiting for security flag to flip. ETA window for activation 2026-03-08 03:00 UTC if peeringOk=true.

Karen (sales): Thanks. I've asked ClearPath to send CID ranges + KMS preference ASAP.

Lucy (eng-platform): I'll wire up the scoped API key creation to the provisioning job so we issue the key simultaneously and attach an allowlist. Also will add cost tagging so finance can attribute usage to the POC.

Security Ops: Once we get CID ranges we'll do a quick review. If they can't provide peering, we can do an IP-only allowlist but we need an attestation from the customer and non-prod SLA.

Karen (sales): All good. Please ping this thread when the change goes live. :raised_hands:

Ajay (eng-runtime): Copy — will monitor p95 latencies and queue depth during the window and report any anomalies to this thread.

Provision Bot: Job pj-20260308-001 will post status updates here when it runs.

Lucy (eng-platform): Scheduled and gated. Will post confirmation when live. :white_check_mark:
